title: Instant asset write-off threshold increases and temporary full expensing
summary: The instant asset write-off rose to $20,000 from 12 May 2015, $25,000 (turnover under $10 million) from 29 January 2019, $30,000 (under $50 million) from 2 April 2019 and $150,000 (under $500 million) from 12 March 2020; temporary full expensing applied from 6 October 2020 to 30 June 2023.

instruments.title: Income Tax Assessment Act 1997, Subdivision 328-D (simplified depreciation), as amended

direction_rationale: Immediate deduction lowers the cost of capital for small firms, raising investment and productivity, though some investment may only be brought forward.
comparison: Firms either side of the turnover caps and asset-cost thresholds (firm-level data); no state variation

verified.notes: Thresholds and dates from the ATO page on depreciation incentives; turnover caps from the ATO depreciating assets guide 2021 (search extract).

assessment.summary: Small and then most businesses could deduct the cost of new equipment immediately, with temporary full expensing from 2020 to 2023. It lowered the cost of capital across the economy, though some investment was brought forward rather than added, and the thresholds and time limits distort which assets and firms benefit.

marks.reason: Immediate deduction lowers the after-tax cost of investing across most industries.
Temporary, threshold-based concessions favour some assets and firm sizes and pull investment forward.

assessment.confidence_note: The Productivity Commission's 2025 report prefers permanent partial expensing to temporary measures.

responsible.note: Administers the Income Tax Assessment Act 1997.

history.what: Temporary full expensing ended; the write-off threshold for small businesses (turnover under $10 million) was set at $20,000 for 2023-24 and 2024-25.
